newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean naphtha buyers suspend trade with Itochu.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean naphtha buyers suspend trade with Itochu.

text.p: Seven South Korean petrochemical companies said they will stop buying naphtha from Itochu Corp, accusing the Japanese trader of price manipulation.
They are Daelim Industrial Co, LG Petrochemical Co, Korea Petrochemical Industry Co, Honam Petrochemical Corp, Samsung General Chemicals Co, Hyundai Petrochemical Co and Hanwha Chemical Corp.
"Current naphtha prices have been totally overvalued and manipulated by one Japanese trader, Itochu Corp," they said in a joint statement seen on Thursday.
Japanese spot quotes had been distorted since last week mainly because of Itochu's purchase of February cargoes despite weaker crude prices and softer European naptha prices, the statement said.

"All companies will suspend physical dealing with the trading company until April arrival cargo, 1997," the statement said. Expanded action would be taken against Itochu if manipulation did not stop, the statement added, without giving any details.
"It does not make sense to be controlled by a company at the expense of most of other industrial partners," it said.
Considering poor chemical product prices and a gloomy future, the "unreasonable and unjustifiable" price of naphtha was imposing a heavy burden, the statement said.
Itochu officials were not immediately available for comment.
